sd.name: Stopping distance
sd.title: Stopping distance
sd.practise: Knowing how far you need to stop at 40, 60 and 80 km/h, dry and wet.
sd.scored: Your guesses (30), stopping before the child in the street (20) and the speed you choose for the road you can see (50). A slower choice never costs a point; a faster one is never rewarded.
sd.controls: Slider or − and + buttons; a full-width BRAKE button (Space or Enter). One hand.
sd.teachingLine: Teaching values: reaction {rt} s, road grip {dry} dry and {wet} wet. Real roads vary.

modes.practiceLine: Three rounds, feedback after each answer
modes.learnLine: The same rounds with a hint on how the distance is made up

sd.noRounds: This session has no rounds to play.

q.street: Pick your speed for this street.
q.react: Tap BRAKE the moment a child steps out.

strip.title: Road from your bike, {kmh} km/h, {surface}
strip.sight: Road to a bend {x} m ahead, {surface}

sd.hint: Before you brake you keep moving for about {rt} s. Braking distance grows with the square of your speed.
sd.result1: You guessed {g} m. Real: about {t} m.
sd.teaching: Teaching values: reaction {rt} s, road grip {mu}. Real roads vary.
sd.typical: No timed tap: use a typical {s} s reaction
sd.early: That was before anything happened. Let's try again.
sd.tooEarly: Braking before anything happens doesn't count as a stop.
sd.noBrake: You didn't brake before reaching the place the child stepped out.
sd.usedTypical: This used a typical reaction time of {s} s, not yours.
sd.stopAt: With that reaction you need {m} m to stop. The child stepped out {child} m ahead.
sd.moving: You'd still be moving at about {kmh} km/h where the child stepped out.
sd.stopped: You stopped about {m} m before the child.

who.below_50: WHO: below 50 km/h the risk to a pedestrian is under 20%.
who.between_50_80: WHO gives no figure between 50 and 80 km/h; at 80 km/h it is about 60%.
who.80_plus: WHO: at 80 km/h the risk to a pedestrian is about 60%.

sd.speedNote: A slower speed gives you more room. It never costs points.
sd.choose: You can see {x} m ahead. What's the fastest you can go and still stop?
sd.needAt: At {kmh} km/h you need about {m} m to stop. You can see {x} m.
sd.tooFast: You'd need more road than you can see.
sd.withinSight: You could stop within the road you can see.
sd.maxSafe: For {x} m of clear road, {kmh} km/h was the most you could stop from.

bs.name: Blind Spot · Trucks and buses
bs.title: Blind Spot
bs.practise: Knowing where a truck driver can't see you, and how to stay out of those zones.
bs.scored: Placing the bike where the driver can see you (30), time out of the blind zones (30), a mirror check before you move (15) and holding back when the truck turns left (25). Passing on the left of a turning truck makes the ride score 0.
bs.controls: Tap a numbered spot, then Place here. On the ride: Move left, Centre, Move right, Mirror check and Hold back (keys ← ↓ → M H). One hand.
bs.zonesNote: Zones vary by vehicle and mirrors; these are illustrative.

modes.learnLine: The same, with the mirror rule before each placement

bs.decisionLink: Decision version: picture choices, no moving game
bs.decisionNote: A different format: you place the bike on a still picture, plan your ride, then watch it play out. Scored the same way, but not the same skill as riding it.
